- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days.
- If true price drops sharply after a peak, model fails to adjust; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 2–4 days to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Model tends to overpredict mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is >75, reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to adjust forecast direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 65, model often underestimates; add 3–7% upward bias for next 5–10 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is negative and true price is rising, model often misses the rebound; increase forecast by 3–6% for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
